title: Pullback of an ample invertible module
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal L$ be an ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] invertible [def-sc-invertible-module] $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $g^*\mathcal L$ be its pullback. Then $g^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Y$.

proof.text: For every $n\ge1$, pullback and tensor product give $(g^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}\cong g^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, and $g^*\mathcal L$ is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. If $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ and $t=g^*s$, the fibre identification in that lemma gives $t(y)=s(g(y))\otimes1$. Extension of a one-dimensional vector space from $\kappa(g(y))$ to $\kappa(y)$ preserves whether a vector is zero. Hence $Y_t=g^{-1}(X_s)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample), part (2), specialized to an affine morphism; nonvanishing equality follows from Modules Lemma Tag 01CT as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor

proof.text: By ampleness of $\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $X$ is quasi-compact and the affine opens $X_s$, with $s$ ranging over global sections of positive tensor powers of $\mathcal L$, cover $X$. Choose finitely many of them covering $X$. Their inverse images $g^{-1}(X_s)=Y_{g^*s}$ cover $Y$ by the previous step; each is affine because the restriction $g^{-1}(X_s)\to X_s$ is affine by base change [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence, clause (1)] and an affine morphism over the affine $X_s$ has affine source [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence, clause (2)]. Thus $Y$ has a finite affine open cover; each affine scheme is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $Y$, a finite union of quasi-compact opens, is quasi-compact, and every point lies in an affine nonvanishing locus of a positive power of $g^*\mathcal L$. By the same ampleness definition, $g^*\mathcal L$ is ample.
